results.reader_what: Clinical trials were treated as filters and signals of innovation, then synthesised and rated for signal strength.
results.reader_more: This review examines recent innovation in psychosocial interventions for reducing violence and aggression in adults. The authors define a conceptual approach in which controlled clinical trials of intervention effectiveness serve as both filters and signals of emerging innovation, citing existing horizon scanning literature for that design. Information extracted from documents identified during filtering is tabulated, findings within and across studies are synthesised and discussed, and the strength of the innovation signal in each study is rated against pre-defined criteria. The clinical framing is anchored in UK NICE definitions and guidance on managing violence and aggression. The horizon scanning method is imported and operationalised for this clinical question rather than advanced as a transferable methodological contribution.

results.reader_more: Backcasting starts from a desired future state and works backwards to identify the steps needed to reach it, in contrast to forecasting from present trends. This article argues the approach has developed along two partly separate tracks, one scholarly and one in planning practice, and synthesises them into a single framework aimed at long-horizon strategic development. results.reader_title: Finland's LUMI AI Factory to host a staged IQM quantum computer built for logical qubits
results.reader_what: CSC will host LUMI-IQ, an IQM superconducting machine delivered in stages from 2027 to 2029.
results.reader_why: Places error-corrected quantum hardware inside a European HPC and AI facility the host institution controls.
results.reader_more: CSC - IT Center for Science in Kajaani will host LUMI-IQ, described as Europe's first superconducting quantum computer designed from the outset to operate with logical qubits. Logical qubits combine several error-prone physical qubits into a more reliable computational unit through quantum error correction. An IQM Halocene H4 system with 150 physical qubits arrives in 2027, with error-correction upgrades in 2028 and a Halocene H5 upgrade in 2029, jointly funded by the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking with Finland, Czechia, Norway and Poland. The machine will be integrated with the LUMI AI Factory's classical HPC and AI resources for hybrid workflows. Nothing has been delivered yet, so the announcement sets out a procurement and a schedule rather than an installed capability.
